PrismaB · Odoo Integration Help

Official API docs: 📄 Download API Documentation (PDF)

1) Connection (Remote Control)

Type: REST · Base URL: https://app.prismab.com

connection_params (JSON):

{
  "username": "user@example.com",
  "password": "*******"
}
  • Get Token calls /api/auth/login and stores bag["token"] (JWT access).
  • Get devices (plan) and Get readings send Authorization: Bearer <token>.

2) Device Discovery and Manual Configuration

For initial setup or when adding new PrismaB devices, use the List Devices procedure to discover available devices and configure them manually in Odoo.

What does this procedure do?

The "PrismaB: List Devices for Support" procedure performs the following actions:

  1. Authenticates with PrismaB API using your credentials
  2. Retrieves all devices available in your PrismaB account from /api/devices
  3. Extracts the device name and prisma_id (UUID) from each device
  4. Generates a simple JSON file with the device list
  5. Attaches the JSON to the Remote Control record for download

This procedure only reads data from PrismaB - it does not create or modify anything in Odoo.

2.5) List Devices Procedure

  1. Get Token → obtain JWT and store it in the bag.
  2. List Devices → call /api/devices and extract device names and prisma_ids into JSON attachment.

3) Default Procedure

  1. Get Token → obtain JWT and store it in the bag.
  2. Get devices (plan) → build bag["sensors_plan"] from device/sensor config.
  3. Get readings → call /api/devices/{prisma_id}/data with date filters and upsert readings.

4) Device Configuration

In each Device (mdm.measurement.device) set remotecontrol_params:

{
  "prisma_id": "b5f7d28c-d7e1-4a7b-a50a-3083c679a4fc",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

5) Sensor Configuration

In each Sensor (mdm.measurement.device.sensor) set remotecontrol_params:

{
  "position": "1",
  "key": "water",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

Complete Configuration Examples

Example: Three soil moisture sensors

Sensor 1 (first ground sensor):

{
  "position": "1",
  "key": "water",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

Sensor 2 (second ground sensor):

{
  "position": "2",
  "key": "water",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

Sensor 3 (third ground sensor):

{
  "position": "3",
  "key": "water",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

6) API Structure & Data Extraction

PrismaB returns data in this format:

[
  {
    "date": "2025-10-13T00:48:25.461Z",
    "deviceId": "b5f7d28c-d7e1-4a7b-a50a-3083c679a4fc",
    "sensors": [
      {                              // ← Position 1 (index 0)
        "kind": "Ground",
        "type": 1,
        "water": 30.098890341760004,
        "conductivity": 0.49,
        "extSat": 2.5528999999999997,
        "temperature": 22.2
      },
      {                              // ← Position 2 (index 1)
        "water": 29.51586281536,
        "temperature": 22.8,
        // ... more parameters
      },
      {                              // ← Position 3 (index 2)
        "water": 34.04090048,
        "temperature": 23.6,
        // ... more parameters
      }
    ]
  }
]

Position Mapping:

  • Position "1" → extracts from sensors[0] (first sensor)
  • Position "2" → extracts from sensors[1] (second sensor)
  • Position "3" → extracts from sensors[2] (third sensor)

7) Time Window & Filtering

  • Get devices (plan) computes initial_date per sensor: last stored reading date → else sensor.start_date → else device.start_date → else Jan 1 of current year.
  • Get readings calls /api/devices/{prisma_id}/data?startDate=YYYY-MM-DD&endDate=YYYY-MM-DD
  • Only readings within time window YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00 to YYYY-MM-DD 23:59:59 are inserted.
  • Timestamps are stored as provided by the API (ISO 8601 UTC format).

Available Parameters in Sensor Data

Use these values in the "key" field of sensor configuration:

Physical Measurements

  • water - Soil moisture/water content (%)
  • temperature - Soil temperature (°C)
  • conductivity - Electrical conductivity
  • extSat - External saturation

Sensor Metadata

  • kind - Sensor type (e.g., "Ground")
  • type - Sensor subtype (numeric)

Complete Configuration Examples

Example 1: Three soil moisture sensors

Device configuration:

  "prisma_id": "b5f7d28c-d7e1-4a7b-a50a-3083c679a4fc",
  "start_date": "2025-10-13"
}

Sensor 1 (first ground sensor):

{

  "key": "water",

}

Sensor 2 (second ground sensor):

Example 2: Mixed parameters from same device

Sensor A (water from first sensor):

{
  "position": "1",
  "key": "water"
}

Sensor B (temperature from second sensor):

{
  "position": "2",

Sensor C (conductivity from third sensor):

{
  "position": "3",
  "key": "conductivity"
}

8) Troubleshooting

  • Missing token error: Ensure "Get Token" action is active and runs first (sequence = 10)
  • No sensors found: Check that sensors have valid remotecontrol_params and are linked to devices
  • Array index errors: Verify position values (1, 2, 3) match available sensors in PrismaB response
  • No readings inserted: Check date window filters and parameter key names

Sequence order: Get Token (10) → Get devices (20) → Get readings (30)

# Get devices from PrismaB resp = request_retry('GET', base_url, headers=headers, timeout=timeout) if resp.status_code >= 400: raise Exception('Error fetching devices: %s %s' % (resp.status_code, resp.text))
devices_data = resp.json() or []
# Build device list extracting from device object devices_list = [] for item in devices_data: if isinstance(item, dict) and 'device' in item: device = item.get('device', {}) device_id = device.get('id') # UUID from device object device_name = device.get('name') or 'Device %s' % device_id if device_id else 'Unnamed Device'
if device_id: devices_list.append({ 'prisma_id': device_id, 'name': device_name }) # Sort by name devices_list.sort(key=lambda x: x['name'])
# Generate JSON report = { 'generated_at': fields.Datetime.now(), 'total_devices': len(devices_list), 'devices': devices_list }
# Create attachment json_str = json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) encoded = base64.b64encode(json_str.encode('utf-8')) fname = 'prismab_devices_%s.json' % fields.Datetime.now()
att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': fname, 'datas_fname': fname, 'datas': encoded, 'mimetype': 'application/json', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id })
